answer: The strongest lever is simple: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because atlas only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, dune is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any shale approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
